segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we're bringing you another elementary level lesson as a part of our interview series.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们将为您带来另一个小学课程，作为我们采访系列的一部分。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: This is part two of the interview series and the last part we talked about, well, a brief introduction when you arrive to a job interview.
segments.zh: 这是面试系列的第二部分，也是我们在面试到达时简要介绍的最后一部分。

segments.en: But on this occasion, we're going to talk a little bit about yourself and your life.
segments.zh: 但在这个场合，我们将谈谈你自己和你的生活。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's the most personal part, I think, of an interview.
segments.zh: 我认为，这是一次采访中最个人化的部分。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to today's dialogue and we'll be back in a moment to talk more about the things that you've heard.
segments.zh: 让我们听听今天的对话，我们稍后会回来更多地谈论你听到的事情。

segments.en: Now, Miss Childs passed on your resume to me and I've had a chance to look it over.
segments.zh: 现在，Childs 小姐将你的简历传递给了我，我有机会查看它。

segments.en: I must say I'm quite impressed.
segments.zh: 我必须说我印象深刻。

segments.en: Thank you very much.
segments.zh: 非常感谢。

segments.en: I've tried to keep it short and clear.
segments.zh: 我试图保持简短和清晰。

segments.en: If there are any questions, please feel free to ask me.
segments.zh: 如果有任何问题，请随时问我。

segments.en: Well, yes, I do have a number of questions, but perhaps first you could give me a brief overview.
segments.zh: 好吧，是的，我确实有很多问题，但也许首先你可以给我一个简短的概述。

segments.en: I'd like to get a little bit of an idea of your background.
segments.zh: 我想了解一下你的背景。

segments.en: Yes, of course.
segments.zh: 是的，当然。

segments.en: Well, as you can see from the resume, I'm 27 and grew up in Brooklyn, New York, although our family moved to London when I was quite young at around 16.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如你从简历中看到的那样，我今年 27 岁，在纽约布鲁克林长大，尽管我们全家在我 16 岁左右的时候搬到了伦敦。

segments.en: Ah, I see.
segments.zh: 啊，我明白了。

segments.en: So you were actually educated in Europe.
segments.zh: 所以你实际上在欧洲接受过教育。

segments.en: Yes, precisely.
segments.zh: 对，正是如此。

segments.en: Although I was born in the US, I would definitely call London home.
segments.zh: 虽然我出生在美国，但我肯定会称伦敦为家。

segments.en: But as you see, I've actually spent a lot of my life moving from country to country.
segments.zh: 但正如你所看到的，我的大部分时间实际上都在从一个国家到另一个国家。

segments.en: My father was in the oil business before he retired, so we also spent a number of years in Saudi Arabia, too.
segments.zh: 我父亲在退休前从事石油业务，所以我们也在沙特阿拉伯呆了几年。

segments.en: Very interesting.
segments.zh: 很有意思。

segments.en: So it seems you had quite an adventurous childhood.
segments.zh: 所以看来你有一个很冒险的童年。

segments.en: Absolutely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: We were never still for too long, but now I'm really looking to settle down.
segments.zh: 我们从没在一个地方待太久，不过现在我真想安定下来了。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, let's move on to discuss your education, shall we?
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们继续讨论你的教育，好吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So obviously this person had a very interesting life and they use some pretty interesting words there.
segments.zh: 所以显然这个人的生活非常有趣，他们在那里使用了一些非常有趣的词。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at five key words that we have prepared for you on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不看看我们在外卖方面为您准备的五个关键词。

segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Alright, so the first word that we have is right when Mr. Parsons talked to Miss Childs and he said that he was very impressed with her resume.
segments.zh: 好吧，当帕森斯先生与柴尔兹小姐交谈时，我们的第一个词是对的，他说他对她的简历印象深刻。

segments.en: Alright, so someone says I'm impressed when they think that something that you did or something about you is very interesting or good or better than most people's.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以有人说当他们认为你所做的事情或关于你的某些事情非常有趣、好或比大多数人的更好时，我会印象深刻。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you're kind of amazed, you're kind of, you're like, wow.
segments.zh: 所以你有点惊讶，你有点，你就像，哇。

segments.en: And so this is an adjective.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个形容词。

segments.en: I am impressed.
segments.zh: 我印象深刻。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So teachers sometimes say this.
segments.zh: 所以老师们有时会这么说。

segments.en: Maybe when you do really, really, really well on a test, they say, hey, Marco, I'm really impressed.
segments.zh: 也许当你在测试中做得非常非常非常好时，他们说，嘿，Marco，我真的印象深刻。

segments.en: You got 99%.
Parents say this to friends, family.
segments.zh: 父母对朋友、家人说这些话。

segments.en: So basically this is a way to say good job.
segments.zh: 所以基本上这是一种说好工作的方式。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And there's also a verb.
segments.zh: 还有一个动词。

segments.en: So this is the adjective to be impressed and the verb form would be to impress someone.
segments.zh: 所以这是要印象深刻的形容词，动词形式会给某人留下深刻印象。

segments.en: So that's obviously if you impress your teacher by studying, your teacher will be impressed.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您通过学习给您的老师留下深刻印象，您的老师会印象深刻。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And following that, Mr. Parson has some questions about Miss Child's background.
segments.zh: 在此之后，帕森先生对孩子的背景有一些疑问。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: He asked her for a brief overview of her background.
segments.zh: 他要求她简要介绍一下她的背景。

segments.en: So we have two interesting words there.
segments.zh: 所以我们有两个有趣的词。

segments.en: An overview.
segments.zh: 概述。

segments.en: What is an overview?
segments.zh: 什么是概述？

segments.en: An overview is like a summary.
segments.zh: 概述就像一个总结。

segments.en: It's basically a way to ask for someone to give you a lot of information in very few words.
segments.zh: 这基本上是一种要求某人用很少的词给你很多信息的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you don't really want too much details.
segments.zh: 所以你真的不想要太多的细节。

segments.en: You don't want somebody to tell you their life in detail.
segments.zh: 你不希望有人详细告诉你他们的生活。

segments.en: You just want a brief summary.
segments.zh: 你只想要一个简短的总结。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So not, I was born on August 11th in 1979 and I was and then I went into this.
segments.zh: 所以不是，我出生于 1979 年 8 月 11 日，然后我进入了这个领域。

segments.en: No, this is basic, simple, you know, this is where I'm from.
segments.zh: 不，这是基本的，简单的，你知道，这就是我来自的地方。

segments.en: This is where I went to school at the end.
segments.zh: 这是我最后去学校的地方。

segments.en: And well, he wanted a brief overview of her background.
segments.zh: 好吧，他想简要概述她的背景。

segments.en: What exactly is her background?
segments.zh: 她的背景到底是什么？

segments.en: Well think about the word back.
segments.zh: 好好想想这个词。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: That means behind or in this case, background is your personal history.
segments.zh: 这意味着在这种情况下或在这种情况下，背景是您的个人历史。

segments.en: So you could ask someone, what's your background?
segments.zh: 所以你可以问别人，你的背景是什么？

segments.en: It means where are you from or you know, what have you been doing up to now in your life?
segments.zh: 这意味着你来自哪里，或者你知道，你现在一直在做什么？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And precisely when he asked her about her background, now she's starting to talk about her life in general terms.
segments.zh: 正是当他问她的背景时，现在她开始笼统地谈论她的生活。

segments.en: As we said, it's an overview.
segments.zh: 正如我们所说，这是一个概述。

segments.en: So she said that she's 27 and she's from Brooklyn, etc.
segments.zh: 所以她说她27岁，来自布鲁克林等。

segments.en: So she starts giving very general information about herself and her life.
segments.zh: 所以她开始提供关于她自己和她的生活的非常笼统的信息。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And when she starts to do this, Mr. Parson has more specific questions about her life because he wants to know details.
segments.zh: 当她开始这样做时，帕森先生对她的生活有更具体的问题，因为他想知道细节。

segments.en: So he asks her then where she was educated.

segments.en: So this this phrase to be educated is very important.
segments.zh: 所以这个要教育的短语非常重要。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So he's asking her, you studied in Europe.

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: To be educated means to have someone teach you or to go to school somewhere.
segments.zh: 接受教育意味着有人教你或去某个地方上学。

segments.en: So for example, I was educated in America.
segments.zh: 例如，我在美国接受教育。

segments.en: Where were you educated, Marco?

segments.en: I was educated in Chile.
segments.zh: 我在智利接受教育。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: So you've been educated in a number of different places, right?
segments.zh: 所以你在许多不同的地方接受过教育，对吧？

segments.en: At home and in a different country.
segments.zh: 在家里和不同的国家。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But you can also specify the university name, right?
segments.zh: 但你也可以指定大学名称，对吧？

segments.en: For example, I was educated at Harvard.
segments.zh: 例如，我在哈佛大学接受教育。

segments.en: Can you say that?
segments.zh: 你能这么说吗？

segments.en: You can.
segments.zh: 你可以。

segments.en: Or I was educated at a number of different schools.
segments.zh: 或者我在许多不同的学校接受过教育。

segments.en: So you can say I studied or I was educated.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说我学习或我受过教育。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, apparently she was moving around from Europe, United States.
segments.zh: 好吧，显然她是从欧洲到美国搬来的。

segments.en: So Mr. Parson says, wow, it seems that you had an adventurous childhood.
segments.zh: 所以帕森先生说，哇，你似乎有一个冒险的童年。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: This is a great adjective, adventurous.
segments.zh: 这是一个很好的形容词，冒险。

segments.en: You can say a person is adventurous.
segments.zh: 你可以说一个人喜欢冒险。

segments.en: So Marco is very adventurous.
segments.zh: 所以马可非常喜欢冒险。

segments.en: He likes to jump out of airplanes.
segments.zh: 他喜欢跳下飞机。

segments.en: But you can also say that an experience is adventurous, like moving around a lot as a child.
segments.zh: 但你也可以说体验是冒险的，就像小时候经常四处走动一样。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So I guess adventurous can go hand in hand with exciting or very interesting, full of emotion.
segments.zh: 所以我想冒险者可以与令人兴奋或非常有趣的、充满情感的人齐头并进。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So adventure, adventurous.
segments.zh: 所以冒险，冒险。

segments.en: So a person can be adventurous.
segments.zh: 所以一个人可以冒险。

segments.en: And we actually had a lesson about this when we describe personalities.
segments.zh: 当我们描述个性时，我们实际上有一个关于此的教训。

segments.en: You can say someone is adventurous.
segments.zh: 你可以说有人喜欢冒险。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So five key words that we just took a look at.
segments.zh: 所以我们只是看了五个关键词。

segments.zh: 我们为什么不回去，再听一次对话，我们会回来多谈谈 Fluency Builder。

segments.zh: 我想了解一下你的背景。

segments.en: Although I was born in the US, I would definitely call London home.

segments.zh: 好的，一开始，帕森斯先生正在继续他在我们第一部分所说的话。

segments.zh: 所以这个动词，传递，这真的很重要。

segments.en: Well, the secretary, Ms. Childs, passed on Rebecca's resume.
segments.zh: 好吧，秘书 Childs 女士通过了 Rebecca 的简历。

segments.en: That basically means she, Ms. Childs received it and she didn't keep it.
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着她，Childs 女士收到了它，而她没有保留它。

segments.en: She passed it on or she gave it to another person.
segments.zh: 她把它传递给了另一个人。

segments.en: In this case, Mr. Parsons.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，帕森斯先生。

segments.zh: 好吧，这意味着，这表明某事不会像你说的那样留在一个人身边，马可，但它会从一个人转移到另一个人。

segments.zh: 好的，这意味着检查或看一看。

segments.zh: 众所周知，她来自布鲁克林，她在布鲁克林长大，然后搬到了伦敦。

segments.en: And so Rebecca described how she spent most of her life moving from country to country.
segments.zh: 因此，丽贝卡描述了她一生中的大部分时间是如何从一个国家到另一个国家的。

segments.en: Okay, from country to country.
segments.zh: 好吧，从一个国家到另一个国家。

segments.en: This means that she moved to many different countries.
segments.zh: 这意味着她搬到了许多不同的国家。

segments.en: Okay, so if I live in America all my life, I never moved from country to country.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以如果我一生都住在美国，我就不会从一个国家搬到另一个国家。

segments.en: You can say this about many different things, from place to place, from town to town.
segments.zh: 你可以说很多不同的事情，从一个地方到另一个地方，从一个城镇到另一个城镇。

segments.en: It means that you live in one, you go from one place to another.
segments.zh: 这意味着你住在一个地方，你从一个地方走到另一个地方。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So as you said, if you replace the noun country, you can say from town to town.
segments.zh: 所以正如你所说，如果你取代了名词国家，你可以说是从一个城镇到另一个城镇。

segments.en: You can even say from house to house.
segments.zh: 你甚至可以说挨家挨户。

segments.en: I went from house to house asking for money.
segments.zh: 我挨家挨户要钱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So from to.
segments.zh: 所以从到。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So from something to something.
segments.zh: 所以从某事到某事。

segments.en: And for our final phrase, she was talking about how she's moved around so much that she's actually ready to settle down.
segments.zh: 对于我们的最后一句话，她说的是她是如何四处走动的，以至于她实际上已经准备好安定下来了。

segments.en: Okay, to settle down.
segments.zh: 好吧，安定下来。

segments.en: This is a really important phrase and I think it's something a lot of people do when they're maybe in their 30s or 40s.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常重要的短语，我认为这是很多人在 30 多岁或 40 多岁时都会做的事情。

segments.en: They don't want to move anymore.
segments.zh: 他们不想再动了。

segments.en: So to settle down means to stay in one place.
segments.zh: 所以安定下来意味着留在一处。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you stay in one place.
segments.zh: 所以你住在一处。

segments.en: And it can have a lot of different meanings as well.
segments.zh: 它也可以有很多不同的含义。

segments.en: For example, to get married, many people say that's settling down.
segments.zh: 例如，为了结婚，许多人说这是安定下来。

segments.en: It means you want to stay in one place and have a family.
segments.zh: 这意味着你想留在一个地方并拥有一个家庭。

segments.en: Or to buy a house because it means that you will live there for a long time.
segments.zh: 或者买房子，因为这意味着你会在那里住很长时间。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So to settle down.
segments.zh: 所以要安定下来。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting phrases there, a lot of words and this is, as we said, part two of our series.
segments.zh: 所以那里有很多有趣的短语，很多单词，正如我们所说，这是我们系列的第二部分。

segments.en: So I think it would be worthy for us to listen to this dialogue one last time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 所以我认为最后一次听这个对话对我们来说是值得的，我们会回来多说一点。

segments.en: Now Miss Childs passed on your resume to me and I've had a chance to look it over.
segments.zh: 现在 Childs 小姐把你的简历传给了我，我有机会看看。

segments.en: I must say I'm quite impressed.
segments.zh: 我必须说我印象深刻。

segments.en: Thank you very much.
segments.zh: 非常感谢。

segments.en: I've tried to keep it short and clear.
segments.zh: 我试图保持简短和清晰。

segments.en: If there are any questions, please feel free to ask me.
segments.zh: 如果有任何问题，请随时问我。

segments.en: Well, yes, I do have a number of questions, but perhaps first you could give me a brief overview.
segments.zh: 好吧，是的，我确实有很多问题，但也许首先你可以给我一个简短的概述。

segments.en: I'd like to get a little bit of an idea of your background.
segments.zh: 我想了解一下你的背景。

segments.en: Yes, of course.
segments.zh: 是的，当然。

segments.en: Well, as you can see from the resume, I'm 27 and grew up in Brooklyn, New York, although our family moved to London when I was quite young at around 16.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如你从简历中看到的那样，我今年 27 岁，在纽约布鲁克林长大，尽管我们全家在我 16 岁左右的时候搬到了伦敦。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: So you were actually educated in Europe.
segments.zh: 所以你实际上在欧洲接受过教育。

segments.en: Yes, precisely.
segments.zh: 对，正是如此。

segments.en: Although I was born in the US, I would definitely call London home.
segments.zh: 虽然我出生在美国，但我肯定会称伦敦为家。

segments.en: But as you see, I've actually spent a lot of my life moving from country to country.
segments.zh: 但正如你所看到的，我的大部分时间实际上都在从一个国家到另一个国家。

segments.en: My father was in the oil business before he retired, so we also spent a number of years in Saudi Arabia too.
segments.zh: 我父亲在退休前从事石油业务，所以我们也在沙特阿拉伯呆了几年。

segments.en: Very interesting.
segments.zh: 很有意思。

segments.en: So it seems you had quite an adventurous childhood.
segments.zh: 所以看来你有一个很冒险的童年。

segments.en: Absolutely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: We were never still for too long, but now I'm really looking to settle down.
segments.zh: 我们从没在一个地方待太久，不过现在我真想安定下来了。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, let's move on to discuss your education, shall we?
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们继续讨论你的教育，好吗？

segments.en: Sure.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So this is part two of a 10-part series of the interviews.
segments.zh: 所以这是采访的 10 部分系列的第二部分。

segments.en: Now we just talked about the background, and I think there are different ways of talking about your background, right?
segments.zh: 现在我们只是谈论背景，我认为谈论你的背景有不同的方式，对吧？

segments.en: This is maybe your personal background.
segments.zh: 这可能是你的个人背景。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you can talk about your personal history, your personal background, where you were born, where you were educated, where you grew up.
segments.zh: 所以你可以谈论你的个人历史、你的个人背景、你出生在哪里、在哪里受过教育、你在哪里长大。

segments.en: But a lot of times we also have to talk about other parts of our background, like our work background or like next week, our educational background.
segments.zh: 但很多时候，我们也不得不谈论我们背景的其他部分，比如我们的工作背景或下周，我们的教育背景。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So part three, we're going to take a look at your educational background.
segments.zh: 所以第三部分，我们将看看你的教育背景。

segments.en: And it's going to be very important because I think in many interviews, people have a hard time describing what they studied or maybe describing exactly what they did during university or college or master's degree or something.
segments.zh: 这将非常重要，因为我认为在许多采访中，人们很难描述他们所学的内容，或者可能准确地描述他们在大学或学院或硕士学位或其他方面所做的事情。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And we're not talking about elementary school or high school.
segments.zh: 我们不是在谈论小学或高中。

segments.en: We're specifically talking about university background here.
segments.zh: 我们在这里专门讨论大学背景。

segments.en: So like you're saying, Marco, what was your major?
segments.zh: 所以就像你说的，马可，你的专业是什么？

segments.en: What was your minor?
segments.zh: 你的未成年人是什么？

segments.en: What was your area of study?
segments.zh: 你的学习领域是什么？

segments.en: These are great, great, great phrases that are very important for an interview.
segments.zh: 这些是伟大的，伟大的，伟大的短语，对面试非常重要。

segments.en: And so we hope that if you have any questions, you'll let us know.
segments.zh: 所以我们希望如果你有任何问题，你会告诉我们的。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com and stay tuned for next week's episode.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 Englishpod.com，请继续关注下周的剧集。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we'll see everyone on the website and until next time.
segments.zh: 所以我们会在网站上见到每个人，直到下一次。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
